Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  March 2, 2023

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on February
2, 2022. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:27 p.m. followed by the
flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Jacob Fragoso
  - District 2, Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4,
  Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Sabrina Barnes  Park, Recreation, and Community Services Director
  Thomas Uwal  Human Services Superintendent
  Gilbert Gonzalez  Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Teresa Estrada  Recreation Superintendent
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

MINUTES. None

STAFF REPORTS.

Amendment No.2 to Agreement No. 21-117 with Bateman Community Living LLC dba
TRIO Community Meals to Provide Food Services for the Elderly Nutrition Program in
Fiscal Year 2022-2023. Staff report dated March 2, 2023, was presented recommending
the Park and Recreation Commission recommend the Mayor and Council members take
the following action: Approve Amendment No. 2 to Agreement No. 21-117 with Bateman
Community Living, LLC, dba TRIO Community Meals, extending the term of the agreement
by one year (with the option to extend one additional year) to provide meals onsite for the
Senior Nutrition Program, in an annual amount not to exceed $795,600, (total contract
amount of $2,386,800). (Grant Fund)

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

It was moved by Commissioner Fragoso and seconded by Commissioner Beck that the
Commission hereby approves the recommendation. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, Beck, and Denmon
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORTS - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. The Graffiti Abatement Supervisor, Gilbert Gonzalez,
reported the following: Installation of a new monument “Splendor of Trees” in the center
area at Edward Vincent Jr. Park commemorating the planting of 56 trees during the 2022
NFL Super Bowl. In addition to regular duties, the wind, and rain has kept staff extremely
busy cleaning up debris in both parks and the center medians. Quite a few tress have fallen,
damaging fencing, and have broken irrigation lines. The Graffiti Abatement team
experienced heavy tagging during the month of February in Districts 1 and 2 constantly
throughout the Hyde Park Blvd. eastbound towards West Blvd. area. Vincent Park
restrooms were also hit massively. North Park has been targeted this past month along
with District 4’s Darby Dixon area including the Crenshaw alleys along 108th Street to
Imperial Highway both north and southbound.

REPORTS - RECREATION. The Recreation Superintendent, Teresa Estrada, reported the
following: Youth Sports Update - both the basketball and soccer leagues are currently in
week 5 and rounding into mid-season form. Our first-year soccer league has been a success
for girls and boys ages 4-7. Picture Day is this Saturday and the season will conclude on
April 1st with our traditional season-ending team celebrations at Shakey’s Pizza involving
food, fun, and awards for all players. Our youth basketball league in partnership with the
Los Angeles Clippers continues to be one of our most exciting programs serving over 300
participants. Teams are now beginning to make significant strides in their fundamental
development, team concepts, and learning to compete while having fun. Playoffs for the
older groups begin the week of April 1st, followed by Championship Saturday, April 8th.
Arguably, our most popular sports offering, Dodgers Dreamteam is ramping up for the
“Spring Season” which begins in April. The Spring Season offers a specific focus on the
younger age groups (5-8) offering T-Ball and Coach Pitch leagues for boys and girls.
Registration is “sold out” for the T-Ball Division while limited space remains available for
the Coach Pitch level. Due to the current construction of two new “Dodgers Dream Fields”
at Edward Vincent Jr. Park, the spring season will take place solely at Darby Park. Come out
to witness the action on Thursday evenings between 5:30 p.m. through 7:45 p.m. and
Saturdays between 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. for more information on our Inglewood Youth
Sports Leagues, visit our city’s sports website at: https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

 REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. The Human Services Superintendent, Thomas Uwal
reported the following: 1) Senior Center Activities and Programs: The Inglewood Senior
Center started a Social Media class that has been well received and filled to capacity.
Another class started at the end of February, A Matter of Balance and it is also filled. The
Voice of Experience monthly newsletter has been re-introduced and is currently in its third
month. It’s a monthly newsletter provided to our seniors so they can stay informed on
Senior Center happenings. Please note, in recognition of Cesar Chavez, the Senior Center
will be closed on March 31, 2023. 2) Nutrition: We are serving approximately 350 seniors
per week through home delivery of meals for seniors homebound and congregate lunches
at our Senior Center, the lunchroom is set up to accommodate safe social distancing. We
also continue to provide fresh produce weekly in collaboration with the Social Justice
Learning Institute. 3) Transportation: Provides trips to critical appointments such as
dialysis and doctors’ appointments as well as leisure trips to locations in and around
Inglewood and Hawthorne. Drivers as well as passengers continue to wear facemasks
during transport. 4) Summer Food and (CACFP) the Child and Adult Care Food Program:
Serves meals to youth 118 years old and under and operates at three sites (Crenshaw
Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park). The CACFP is on hold while we contract a food
vendor. The program’s hours are Monday through Friday, providing supper from 2:30 p.m.
- 3:30 p.m. and snacks from 4:30 p.m. - 5:30 p.m., serving an average of 70 meals per day
at all three sites. We hope to provide more meals once we have a new vendor to benefit
the youth of our community. We are currently working with the Inglewood Unified School
District (IUSD) to reestablish the After-School Program (ASRP) and will know in the coming
weeks which schools will participate.

REPORTS - DIRECTOR. We are developing specifications at Rogers Park to add fitness
stations. We also have some funding to upgrade some fencing and add some bleachers.
The Clippers, as a part of their agreement with the city, have several community benefit
items that will come to the city. They are committed to renovating basketball courts in the
City of Inglewood, not just the courts at the parks but their mission is to renovate all
basketball courts throughout the city including the school district’s courts, the city’s courts,
non-profit courts. Wherever they can make an impact, they plan to do that. FYI, this
includes indoor courts as well.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Brown would like to note that some of the
comments were inspiring and announced there will be some good upcoming events
happening at the Senior Center. Commissioner Denmon announced he‘d be celebrating
his 50th wedding anniversary.

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 7:01 p.m.
